subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: Returns in E-Commerce
description: A quick, practical guide to Returns in E-Commerce.

hook.text: Buy three sizes, keep one, return two. Free returns make this rational—for the customer, not the retailer.

buildup.text: E-commerce return rates are 20–30%, triple that of brick-and-mortar. Reverse logistics is exploding.

discovery.text: Processing a return costs $10–20: shipping, inspection, restocking, or disposal. Most items lose value.

twist.text: Free returns drive sales—but they also drive losses. Some retailers now charge for returns.

climax.text: Zara, H&M, and Amazon have all introduced return fees. The era of unconditional free returns is ending.

punchline.text: Free returns aren't free. Someone always pays.

quiz.question: How much does processing an e-commerce return typically cost?
